title: The Impact of Increase in Minimum Wages on Consumer Perceptions of Service: A Transformer Model of Online Restaurant Reviews
authors: Dinesh Puranam; Vrinda Kadiyali; Vishal Narayan
eligible_reason: Not eligible. Single adoption date: the San Jose minimum-wage increase (March 2013) treats every San Jose zip code in the same month (city_post first equals 1 at Trend 15 for all 28 treated zips in the independent-restaurant file), with other Bay Area zips as controls. Estimated with gsynth interactive fixed effects (generalized synthetic control) with review-level covariates, not TWFE.
design_notes: Main Models/Original Replication Submission.ipynb (R kernel): gsynth(prob ~ city_post + rev_len + Restaurant.ID + Review.ID + Reviewer.ID, index = c('Group','Trend'), force = 'two-way', estimator = 'ife', CV = TRUE, r up to 9 factors, AR = 1), zipcode-month panel of mean transformer-classified review-topic probabilities, 12-month window around the increase (Table 5); Border Effects notebook repeats for border zips (Table 6). Data check (python3 -I): 34 zips, Trend 0-29; city_post adoption at Trend 15 for all treated zips (one zip at 16 in the chain file because its month-15 row is missing).
data_files_note: Zipcode-month aggregates of Yelp review classifications shipped; the transformer classification step is not included.
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available locally (data/text/mksc and papers/mksc checked Nov 2); the OpenAlex abstract in data/frame/mksc.jsonl is a one-sentence summary. Design read from the README and the main-results code; no package code was run.
